payload.reasoning_summary: FASE-1 is the earliest incomplete phase. The nominal fixed-point types and scale constants are an unimplemented, dependency-free foundation required by domain, world, and application work. The proposal is accepted with corrected runtime expectations: TypeScript brands are compile-time constructs, so cross-brand misuse must be rejected by type tests rather than runtime brand inspection.
risks: TypeScript brands provide compile-time nominal separation only and cannot authenticate a brand after type erasure; runtime validation must therefore validate primitive representation and numeric bounds.
Constructor naming and export shape must remain minimal and consistent to avoid creating an accidental public API that later FASE-1 work must preserve.

acceptance_criteria: packages/core publicly exports distinct Money, Quantity, Price, Rate, and Tick types; assigning any one branded type to another fails the compile-time type test.
Money, Quantity, Price, and Rate have bigint as their underlying representation, while Tick has number as its underlying representation.

The Tick constructor accepts exactly safe integers in the inclusive range [Number.MIN_SAFE_INTEGER, Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER] and rejects fractional numbers, NaN, infinities, and values outside that range.
Runtime constructors reject values whose primitive type does not match the represented type; no acceptance criterion requires detecting an already-erased incorrect TypeScript brand at runtime.
packages/core publicly exports QUANTITY_SCALE as 100000000n, PRICE_SCALE as 10000n, and RATE_SCALE as 100000000n without floating-point conversion.
No production implementation uses Math.random, Date, performance, crypto entropy, floating-point arithmetic, or mutable global state.
The repository compile, lint, test, and dependency-boundary commands all exit successfully.
must_preserve: CanonicalEncoder behavior and its accepted test vectors remain unchanged.
All existing determinism lint rules remain green.
The existing dependency graph remains green; packages/core must not acquire imports from higher-layer packages.
All existing strict TypeScript compiler settings remain enabled.
task.objective: Provide the locked nominal bigint types, safe Tick type, constructors, and fixed-point scale constants required by FASE-1 consumers.
out_of_scope: Rounding helpers, division enforcement, or ADR-004.
Ledger, transaction, order, pricing, tick-loop, Electron, worker, CI installer, or packaging work.
Runtime detection of cross-brand values, because TypeScript brands are erased at runtime.
Changes to CICLO_SPEC.md or unrelated packages.
required_tests: Unit tests for every exported constructor and scale constant.
Tick boundary tests covering Number.MIN_SAFE_INTEGER, Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, both adjacent out-of-range values, fractional values, NaN, and positive and negative infinity.
Compile-time negative tests using the repository's established TypeScript type-test mechanism for every relevant cross-brand assignment and unbranded primitive assignment.
Run the full existing test suite, TypeScript compilation, lint suite, and dependency-boundary check.
scope: Define and export Money, Quantity, Price, and Rate as distinct branded bigint types from packages/core.
Define and export Tick as a distinct branded number type.
Add constructors that validate runtime input types and reject invalid Tick values, including non-integers and values outside the JavaScript safe-integer range.
Export QUANTITY_SCALE = 100000000n, PRICE_SCALE = 10000n, and RATE_SCALE = 100000000n as bigint constants.
Add compile-time type assertions proving that the nominal types are not mutually assignable.
Expose the new public API through the existing packages/core entry point.
